title: Isolar os testes de dispatch do supervisor (implementer e demais fases) do project.toml vivo, no padrao CAM-405, para backend codex ser config commitavel
description: O CAM-405 criou o seam de configPath so para makeReviewDispatch (reviewer). Commitar [backend] implementer = codex quebrou o CI com 85 fails (medido no PR #333, run 30187674682): os testes de runSupervisor (loop.test.ts e familia) leem o project.toml vivo via readPhaseBackend/readPhaseModel sem configPath, entao um tree com backend codex faz o dispatch de teste resolver codex, falhar o auth preflight fail-closed na maquina de CI sem codex auth, e quebrar asserts de spawn-resolution/claude-backed. Fix: estender o seam de configPath (ou injecao equivalente) a TODOS os sites de resolucao de fase consumidos por teste (implementer no loop.ts, planner/auditor no plan-runner, run.ts), com teste de regressao provando que um config codex-resolving nao quebra a suite generica, no mesmo desenho do CAM-405. Desbloqueia: re-aplicar implementer=codex (gpt-5.6-sol) como config commitada; o backend codex ja provou funcionar ao vivo (11/11 stories DONE round-a-round no ciclo CAM-406). Reverter aplicado em ea72a1da deve ser desfeito quando isto shipar.

spec.scope:
Extend the CAM-405 `configPath` injection seam to the three remaining production phase-resolution sites that read the live scripts/cam/project.toml, isolate the generic supervisor and plan-runner test suites onto fixture configs, and then re-commit `[backend] implementer = "codex"` (undoing revert ea72a1da) with green CI as the acceptance evidence.

MEASURED CENSUS (verified by two independent read-only sweeps; do not re-derive). Exactly THREE dispatch sites are un-seamed, which is SIX reader calls, since each site does readPhaseBackend then resolvePhaseModel back-to-back:
  1-2. src/supervisor/loop.ts:1108 readPhaseBackend('implementer') and :1118 resolvePhaseModel({phase:'implementer'}), both inside runSupervisor.
  3-4. src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts:655 readPhaseBackend('planner') and :658 resolvePhaseModel({phase:'planner'}), both inside resolveAndSpawnPlanner.
  5-6. src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts:731 readPhaseBackend('auditor') and :734 resolvePhaseModel({phase:'auditor'}), both inside resolveAndSpawnAuditor.
ALREADY SEAMED, these are templates and not work: review.ts:394,404 (CAM-405); run.ts:626,627,639 (CAM-425); orch-resolve.ts:74,75,81; config.ts:299,300.

NO signature change is needed anywhere in src/config/: the readers already accept the seam. readPhaseModel(phase, configPath?, backend?) models.ts:158; readPhaseEffort(phase, configPath?) models.ts:197; readBackend(configPath?) models.ts:224; readPhaseBackend(phase, configPath?) models.ts:265; resolvePhaseModel({phase, backend, configPath?, cacheReader?}) model-resolution.ts:145. Each defaults via defaultProjectConfigPath() = join(process.cwd(),'scripts','cam','project.toml') at models.ts:89-91, which is cwd-relative at call time with no upward search. That is precisely why today's tests must chdir, and why the seam is the correct fix rather than more chdir helpers.

REQUIRED OUTCOMES.
R1. RunSupervisorOptions (src/supervisor/loop.ts:205) gains an optional configPath, threaded to loop.ts:1108 and :1118, documented in the doc-comment style of MakeReviewDispatchOptions.configPath (review.ts:283-299).
R2. RunPlanPhaseOptions (plan-runner.ts:286) gains the same optional configPath, threaded through runPlannerSpawnStep (:1015, invocation :1025) and runAuditorSpawnStep (:1036, invocation :1046) down to the four plan-runner reader calls.
R3. The generic implementer and plan-runner test suites default to a module-level real-tmpdir fixture config declaring the claude backend, in the shape of review.test.ts:268-286 plus :343-350, including the `'configPath' in overrides` opt-out so existing chdir-based tests keep deliberately exercising the live-default path.
R4. One AC5-style codex regression test per newly seamed phase, modelled on review.test.ts:2008.
R5. `[backend] implementer = "codex"` is re-committed to scripts/cam/project.toml, sequenced as the LAST story.

BLAST RADIUS of the test isolation. Implementer: about 168 runSupervisor invocations across 12 files, led by test/supervisor/loop.test.ts (120), then implement-blocked-marker-wiring (9), non-convergence-terminal (8), notify-orchestrator (6), events (5), pause-halt (4), loop-model-resolution (4), ensure-worker-pane (3), test/notify/resend (3), test/logging/spawn-resolution (3), pause-resume (2), suggestion-filing-hook (1). Planner and auditor: about 158 plan-phase invocations across 15 files, led by test/supervisor/plan/plan-runner.test.ts (44), plan-runner-replan (31), plan-runner-container (21), test/plan-runner-target-invalid (10), test/supervisor/plan-runner (9), plan-runner-codex-auth (8), plan-runner-auditor-payload (8), plan-runner-model-resolution (6), test/plan-runner-no-prd (6), plan-runner-target-prompt (5), plan-runner-in-progress-conflict (5), integration/plan-runner-target-obey (2), plus three files with one each. Today only about 6 of loop.test.ts's 120 invocations isolate at all, via process.chdir helpers at loop.test.ts:172 and :4251, plan-runner-codex-auth.test.ts:105 and plan-runner-model-resolution.test.ts:124.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: RunSupervisorOptions exposes an optional configPath string field, and both src/supervisor/loop.ts:1108 (readPhaseBackend) and :1118 (resolvePhaseModel) receive it. When configPath is omitted the resolved backend and model are byte-for-byte identical to current behavior, because the readers apply their own default. Do NOT introduce a local `??` default at the site: match the review.ts:370-373 pattern where the local is simply the possibly-undefined option.

AC2: RunPlanPhaseOptions exposes the same optional configPath string field, and all four plan-runner reader calls (:655, :658, :731, :734) receive it, threaded from the exported entrypoints runPlanPhase (:1121) and runPlanPhaseWithReplan (:1260) through runPlannerSpawnStep and runAuditorSpawnStep. Omission preserves current behavior byte-for-byte.

AC3: The private helpers resolveAndSpawnPlanner (plan-runner.ts:638) and resolveAndSpawnAuditor (plan-runner.ts:714) currently take 11 positional parameters. Threading may add a parameter or convert them to an options object; growing them to a 12th positional is a legitimate reason to prefer the options object. Whichever is chosen, no call site outside plan-runner.ts changes shape.

AC4: A module-level real-tmpdir fixture config (mkdtempSync, containing at minimum a [backend] section naming claude) is defaulted into the generic implementer test suites via the `'configPath' in overrides ? overrides.configPath : GENERIC_FIXTURE_PATH` idiom, with afterAll cleanup. The existing chdir-based tests opt out with an explicit `configPath: undefined` so they keep covering the live-default path on purpose.
AC5: The same generic-fixture default is applied to the generic plan-runner test suites covering the planner and auditor phases, with the same explicit opt-out for the chdir-based tests.

AC6: Three new codex regression tests, one per newly seamed phase (implementer, planner, auditor). Each stages a tmpdir project.toml selecting the codex backend for that phase plus a [models.codex] pin, injects a faked auth check, and asserts: the auth check was called, the dispatch did not return an error whose detail contains 'codex-auth-failed', and the dispatched command carries the pinned codex model. Modelled on test/supervisor/review.test.ts:2008.

AC7: Each of the three AC6 tests is swept red against a tree without the corresponding seam, and the red result is reported in the story handoff. A seam test that passes without the seam is a tautological oracle and does not count as verification.

AC8: scripts/cam/project.toml contains `implementer = "codex"` under [backend], restoring what ea72a1da removed. The pre-existing [models.codex] implementer = "gpt-5.6-sol" pin is left untouched. This is the last story in the PRD.

AC9: bun run typecheck is clean, bun test is fully green with the AC8 config flip applied, and bun run check:all passes. No new test uses skipIf. Green CI on the PR that carries the AC8 flip is the acceptance evidence for the issue as a whole; a green CI on a claude-only config proves nothing new and is not acceptable evidence.
gotchas: CORRECTION TO INHERITED CONTEXT: the prior orchestrator handoff and the CAM-425 journal entry both name test/commands/run-configpath-seam.test.ts as the regression-test model. That is WRONG and must not be followed. Its fixture has no [backend] section at all, so readBackend falls through to DEFAULTS.backend='claude'; its cacheReader is never injected or invoked; it asserts only that a staged model and effort reach the argv. It proves path isolation on a claude-resolving fixture and proves nothing about codex safety.

The correct model is test/supervisor/review.test.ts, which pairs TWO mechanisms that must BOTH be reproduced. Mechanism (a), the module-level generic fixture at :268-286 defaulted in by makeDispatchOpts at :343-350, is what actually makes the committed config safe to flip. Mechanism (b), the AC5 codex regression at :2008, is what makes the seam falsifiable. Shipping the seam plus (b) without (a) leaves CI just as red as it is today.

NO control-flow reordering is required at any of the three sites, and this must not be re-litigated. Misreading resolve/preflight/build ordering as chronological is exactly what escalated the CAM-398 plan through two audit rounds. Grounding here shows the caller's opts object is already in lexical scope at every resolution point: in runSupervisor, opts.codexModelsCacheReaderFn is already read ten lines below the site at :1121; in plan-runner, opts is already destructured at :1021 and :1042.

Both enclosing options interfaces are already dependency-injection-shaped and already carry sibling seams of exactly this kind: codexAuthCheckFn, codexModelsCacheReaderFn, preflightContainerFn, escalateFn. This is an additive field on an established pattern, not a new architecture.

MEASURED CI FAILURE MECHANISM, not inferred: 85 fails on PR #333, GitHub Actions run 30187674682. Chain: live toml resolves implementer to codex at loop.ts:1108, resolvePhaseModel yields gpt-5.6-sol from [models.codex] and passes the static claude-alias guard at codex-auth.ts:154, then codexAuthPreflight at loop.ts:1285 with no injected authCheck reads the real ~/.codex/auth.json at codex-auth.ts:149, the CI runner is unauthenticated, proceed is false, lastOutcome becomes blocked and no respawn-pane happens, so every test asserting status complete, spawn argv, or spawn-resolution backend claude flips red.

Revert ea72a1da removed only `implementer = "codex"` from [backend] (1 file, 1 deletion) and deliberately KEPT the [models.codex] pin, which is harmless while no phase resolves to codex because readNestedBackendModel returns undefined when backend is not codex (models.ts:111-125). The same disease was previously reverted three times on the reviewer phase (04abdb4a, eae0c5f6, e6e46192), which is what motivated CAM-405 in the first place.

Two canary tests directly encode the live-config dependency and will need the fixture treatment: test/supervisor/loop-model-resolution.test.ts:269-289 asserts that with no chdir the repo's own project.toml resolves the implementer backend to claude (asserting cacheReaderCalled is false), and the same dependency exists at plan-runner-codex-auth.test.ts:246 and plan-runner-model-resolution.test.ts:289. An in-code comment at loop-model-resolution.test.ts:132-136 states the constraint verbatim.

NON-GOAL N1: do NOT thread readPhaseEffort at these three sites. Measured fact: readPhaseEffort is called ONLY from the two orchestrator sites (run.ts:639, orch-resolve.ts:81). The implementer, planner and auditor phases never read [efforts]. Adding it is scope creep with no consumer.

NON-GOAL N2: do NOT modify the already-seamed sites (review.ts, run.ts, orch-resolve.ts, config.ts). NON-GOAL N3: do NOT change any signature in src/config/, since the readers already accept configPath.

OUT OF SCOPE but measured this session and worth a separate follow-up issue rather than a story here: run.ts:584 calls buildOrchestratorBootPrompt() with no argument, and that function (run.ts:225-226) forwards to readMetaLoop(configPath), so the boot prompt's meta-loop read still bypasses the CAM-425 seam. Also out of scope: the stale comment at test/commands/run-model-resolution.test.ts:126 still claiming there is no configPath seam.

Naming asymmetry to be aware of, not to fix: the review seam uses readPhaseBackend('reviewer', configPath) while the run seam uses the global readBackend(opts.configPath), documented as deliberate at run.ts:610-613. The three sites in scope here are all per-phase, so they follow the review.ts form.
CI runs `bun run check:all -- --json` per .github/workflows/ci.yml:26, so the AC8 flip is exercised by the exact gate that went red before.
domainTerms: configPath seam: an optional configPath field on an already-DI-shaped options interface, threaded to the phase-resolution readers so a test can point resolution at a fixture project.toml instead of the live scripts/cam/project.toml. Introduced by CAM-405 on MakeReviewDispatchOptions, extended by CAM-425 to run.ts.

phase-resolution site: a place in production code where a dispatch resolves the backend and model (and sometimes effort) for one LLM phase, by calling readPhaseBackend/readBackend followed by resolvePhaseModel immediately before building the spawn argv.

generic fixture default: the review.test.ts:343-350 idiom where a test-options builder defaults configPath to a module-level tmpdir fixture, using `'configPath' in overrides` so an explicit undefined is an opt-out rather than a fallback to the default.
tautological oracle: a test assertion that passes both with and without the change under test, and therefore verifies nothing. Guarded against here by AC7's red-sweep requirement.

fail-closed auth preflight: codexAuthPreflight refuses to dispatch when the codex backend is selected but no valid ~/.codex/auth.json is readable. Correct in production, and the direct cause of the 85 CI failures when tests resolve codex on an unauthenticated runner.
